title: azboard/1
description: A whiteboard of code: cutouts of source files (a picture of some lines, with the path, the lines, a hash of them, the revision they were circled at and a permalink to them there) and the arrows between them, with a history of snapshots that say why the architecture is shaped the way it is. Written by AzReview; read by it and by any viewer. A reader ignores a field it does not know and leaves out an item of a kind it does not know; it refuses a document whose format names a newer major version. See azboard.md.

format.description: The name and the major version of the format. A reader of version 1 refuses azboard/2 and later.

generator.description: The program that wrote the document and its version, for a person to read.

board.description: Which board of its workspace this is.

id.description: Stable among the boards of the workspace.

modified_ms.description: Unix milliseconds: when the board was last kept, or exported.

workspace.description: The folder the code was in: its own name, never its path on the machine.

path_in_repo.description: Where the folder lies inside the repository, with '/' and none at either end. Absent when it is the repository's own folder. The paths of the items are the repository's own: this is what is taken off to get the folder's.

author.description: The name the board is written with: the name git is configured with (never the e-mail address), or the one the setting whiteboard-author gives. Absent when the setting is off or git has no name.

canvas.description: The coordinates of the items: px, x grows to the right, y downwards from the top-left corner; the origin is arbitrary and the canvas has no edge.

view.description: How the person last looked at the canvas: the pan (the canvas point at the panel's top-left corner, in px) and the zoom.

bounds.description: The rectangle that holds every cutout and every free end of an arrow: where a viewer fits the picture. Derived; a reader may ignore it.

next_id.description: An id no item of this board has had: ids are never given twice on a board, so an id names one item for ever.

assets.description: The pictures, by id. A cutout names its picture here.

items.description: What is on the board, in the order it is drawn (the last is on top).

snapshots.description: The history of the board: save points that are never changed once written, oldest first, each with the reason it was taken.

path.description: A relative path of plain segments: no '..', no '.', no empty segment, no backslash, no drive.

rev.description: A full commit hash: 40 hex digits (SHA-1) or 64 (SHA-256), lower case.

repo.description: The git repository the code is in, as far as it is known; absent for a folder that is no repository (then there are no links, only paths and lines).

remote.description: The remote as git says it, without a password or token in it.

web_url.description: The remote as a web address: https://github.com/owner/repo.

host.description: Which form a link to a line takes.

rev.description: The commit the folder was at when the document was written.

branch.description: A hint: the branch HEAD was on.

dirty.description: Whether the working tree had changes that were not committed (files git tracks). Absent when it was not looked at.

width.description: In pixels of the picture itself.

src.description: A data: address (data:image/png;base64,...), or a name relative to the document: a file beside it, or an entry of the archive the document is kept in. Never an address on the web: a reader does not fetch one.

kind.description: cutout or arrow; a reader leaves out a kind it does not know.

id.description: Stable and never given twice on the board.

cutout.description: A picture of some lines of a file, with where they came from.

x.description: The top-left corner on the canvas.

width.description: How large the cutout is shown on the canvas.

label.description: What the person wrote under it.

asset.description: A key of the document's assets.

scale.description: Device pixels of the picture for one px of the canvas: the picture is shown width/scale of the canvas wide.

image_state.description: Why there is no picture: it was not drawn yet, or could not be.

source.description: The lines of code a cutout shows.

path.description: Relative to the repository's root (to the workspace's folder when it is no repository).

hash.description: The SHA-256 of the covered lines, each followed by a line feed (a carriage return at the end of a line is not part of it), as UTF-8: cut the lines out of the file at 'rev', write a line feed after each, hash. All the covered lines, also when 'code' holds fewer.

rev.description: The commit the lines were circled at. Absent when it was not known; then there is no permalink.

permalink.description: The address of these lines at 'rev' on the repository's host (GitHub: https://github.com/owner/repo/blob/REV/PATH#L10-L20; GitLab, Bitbucket and Gitea have their own forms; another host the template of the settings, else GitHub's). A link that names a commit shows the same lines for ever.

language.description: By the file's name, for colouring the code.

code.description: The lines as the board kept them (at most 200 lines of 300 characters): what a viewer shows and searches.

azreview.description: What only AzReview itself uses (the page of the file the loop was drawn on, its outline, two quick hashes); another reader leaves it alone.

arrow.description: An arrow from one end to another, the head at 'to'.

bend.description: 0 is straight; the sign says to which side it curves.

end.description: Fastened to an item (it follows it), or loose at a point of the canvas.

anchor.description: Where on the cutout: auto (where the line to the other end meets its edge), the middle of a side, or a point given as fractions of its width and height.
